title: Transportation technology grants can create local demonstration capacity before usable public service is proven
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107841 review of the Department of Transportation Strengthening Mobility and Revolutionizing Transportation (SMART) grants program
geography: United States; SMART grant applicants and selected projects from fiscal years 2022–2024

observations.period: First three years of SMART applications; awards through September 2025

denominator.unit: SMART grant applications received; applicants included communities of different sizes, entity types, and technology areas

announced_award_amount.unit: millions of U.S. dollars; about 58% of the $500 million authorized and appropriated for FY2022–FY2026 before the later transfer

completion.value: most projects were not yet completed

observations.method: GAO reviewed DOT data on applicants and selected projects from fiscal years 2022–2024, interviewed DOT officials, and interviewed 17 selected recipients covering community sizes and technology areas.
observations.uncertainty: The report describes program applications, awards, recipient-reported implementation challenges, and DOT's learning process; it does not provide a national estimate of completed deployments, service quality, safety, travel time, access, or household benefit.
observations.subgroup: State, city, and tribal government recipients across eight advanced-transportation technology areas; the 17 interviewed recipients are selected rather than a representative sample.
observations.counterinterpretation: A project that was incomplete at the review date may later become operational, and a demonstration can produce valuable learning before it delivers regular public service. Procurement delay alone does not establish project failure.

observations.period: Program implementation and learning process; report published March 2026

denominator.unit: selected SMART grant recipients interviewed by GAO

procurement_delay.value: recipients reported difficulty procuring necessary technology and equipment, affecting project timeframes

lessons_learned.value: DOT had collected project information but had not fully aligned its efforts with key practices for analyzing, validating, documenting, and disseminating lessons

recommendation.unit: open GAO recommendation to develop and implement a SMART lessons-learned plan

observations.method: GAO interviews with 17 selected recipients and DOT officials, review of DOT program information, and comparison with GAO and federal guidance on lessons-learned processes.
observations.uncertainty: Interview evidence identifies implementation and management conditions but does not measure which specific delays changed final service, safety, reliability, or adoption outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Selected recipients and DOT program administration; effects may differ by technology, procurement market, community capacity, and project scale.
observations.counterinterpretation: A centralized lessons-learned process may improve later adoption, but it cannot substitute for project completion, operating performance, or evidence that residents and workers can use the resulting service.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO report supplies SMART application, award, completion-status, recipient-interview, procurement, and lessons-learned findings.

boundary: This record establishes a grant-to-demonstration and program-learning boundary. It does not establish completed public deployment, actual passenger or worker use, safety, reliability, affordability, access, local acceptance, emissions, or household mobility outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO HTML report page retrieved and hashed; full report, project files, and local service records not retained
